summary: A compact earbud shell must hold molded parts, acoustic components and electronics in a repeatable assembly. When ultrasonic welding is selected, joint geometry, resin, fixture support, tooling contact and process settings influence seam appearance and consistency. This iSoud guide helps private label buyers turn shell assembly into clear OEM/ODM review questions.

sections.title: Why shell joining should be reviewed before cosmetic approval
body: Ultrasonic-welding guidance from Toman ThermoSonics describes joint design as a critical part of the molded component, with butt, step, shear and tongue-and-groove configurations selected around material, geometry, weld needs and cosmetic appearance. Emerson Branson also positions process control as important for small and intricate plastic assemblies.

For an earbuds buyer, the practical point is simple: a perfect color chip does not prove that the final welded shell will have an acceptable seam. The approved sample should use production-intent resin, molded joint features, fixture support, internal parts and surface finish.

sections.title: Shell-assembly RFQ questions for an earphone factory
bullets: Which shell parts are welded, bonded, snapped or mechanically retained?
What joint geometry and molded energy-directing feature are used for the selected resin?
How does the fixture support the shell without marking the visible custom finish?
Which weld parameters and process signals are recorded for pilot and production units?
How are seam gap, step, flash, whitening, cracking and surface marks inspected?
How are microphones, drivers, mesh, batteries and circuit boards protected during joining?
Which destructive or functional checks are used to confirm the approved process window?

sections.title: Joint geometry, tooling and internal parts work as one system
body: Toman's guidance explains that an energy director concentrates initial contact so material melts and flows through the joint. Telsonic's electronics-housing example also highlights material choice, seam design, vibration load and process monitoring when delicate components sit inside a plastic assembly.

The buyer should therefore avoid approving an empty cosmetic shell as the only reference. Internal supports, wires, adhesive, acoustic paths and component position can affect how the assembled product responds during joining.
bullets: Use production-intent molded parts and internal components for approval.
Define visible keep-clear zones for tooling and fixture contact.
Inspect seam appearance around microphones, vents and touch areas.
Retain process settings with the signed sample identity.
Repeat validation after resin, colorant, tooling or joint changes.

sections.title: Custom color and coating can change seam visibility
body: A dark gloss, light matte, metallic effect or translucent shell can reveal seam mismatch differently. Coating thickness and surface texture can also change fixture contact or make minor flash more visible. Cosmetic and assembly approval should therefore happen on the final CMF direction.

faq: What should a buyer ask an earbud shell assembly factory?
Ask about joining method, joint geometry, resin, fixtures, process records, internal-component protection, seam limits and production-intent validation samples.
Can an empty shell sample approve the final welding result?
It may show appearance, but final approval should use production-intent internal parts, resin, tooling support and assembly settings.
Can custom color affect visible shell seams?
Color, gloss, texture and coating can change how gaps, steps, flash or fixture marks appear, so assembly and CMF should be approved together.
